docs.text: ACME Client Dialog Guide The ACME Client communicates with an ACME directory to manage an account, create certificate orders, complete authorizations, and retrieve issued certificates. It exposes individual ACME commands and a guided Issue Certificate workflow. Figure 1. ACME Client dialog. Retrieve the directory first to populate endpoint commands, then build and send requests while parsing server responses. Screen Areas Use CertMan — Select whether the ACME account key comes from CertMan or KeyPairMan. The client supports RSA, ECDSA, and EdDSA account keys. ACME URL / Directory / Clear — Enter the ACME directory URL and select Directory to retrieve its endpoint map. The command selector is populated from the directory response. Clear clears saved URL entries. Cert ID / Issue Certificate — Cert ID identifies a certificate for applicable commands. Issue Certificate runs the guided account, order, authorization, challenge, finalize, and certificate retrieval sequence, prompting before each step. Link tab — Contains Nonce URL , Location , and KID . Get Nonce fetches a Replay-Nonce; GetLocation retrieves the selected resource; Get PubKey loads the account key's public-key identifier. Nonce automatic change allows the nonce to be refreshed during command processing. User tab — Enter the account Email and add DNS identifiers to the DNS list. DNS Check opens DNS checking for the listed names. Add and Clear manage the identifier list. ChallTest opens the challenge test utility. Command tab — Select an ACME command, enter or confirm its endpoint URL, and choose Make to create the signed JSON request. The hash selection is used with the account key. Auth List / Challenge List / Order List — Display parsed authorizations, challenges, and orders. Their context menus provide available row operations, including removal or rebuilding where supported. Method / Auto Send / Send — Choose POST or GET . Auto Send transmits a generated request automatically; otherwise use Send manually. Thumb Print / Deactivate / UpdateAccount — Run account/key actions for the selected ACME context. Request — Displays the JSON/JWS request. Verify checks its JWS signature; View opens the JSON structure; C clears it. HTTP Status shows the response status associated with the request exchange. Response / Parser / Auto / Status — Displays the server's JSON or Base64 response. Parser interprets the response and updates command, authorization, challenge, or order lists. Auto parses responses automatically. View inspects the response structure; C clears it. Clear All / Close — Clear the current ACME state or close the dialog. Start an ACME Session Enter the ACME directory URL and select Directory . The directory endpoints and nonce URL are loaded into the command controls. Select an account key source with Use CertMan . The first signed request prompts for the account key pair or certificate/key from the selected manager. Select Get Nonce or leave Nonce automatic change enabled to manage nonces during requests. Enter the account email in the User tab and add the DNS identifier to the list. Choose a command and review the endpoint URL. Select Make to build the signed request. With Auto Send enabled, it is sent immediately. Review the HTTP status and response. Keep Auto enabled or select Parser to extract endpoint links and populate the command, authorization, challenge, and order lists. Issue a Certificate Retrieve the directory and nonce, enter the account email, and add one DNS name. The guided workflow currently supports one DNS identifier at a time. Select Issue Certificate and confirm each prompted command. The workflow creates an account and order, processes authorization and challenge steps, finalizes the order, fetches the order/certificate, and displays the returned certificate chain. Complete the DNS or HTTP challenge with the validation data required by the ACME server. Use DNS Check or ChallTest where appropriate; this dialog does not make control of the domain automatic. When prompted, save the issued certificate and private key to CertMan. Command and Response Handling Directory fetches the server's directory object and fills the endpoint list. Make constructs the request for the selected command; Send transmits it using the selected HTTP method. Parser reads the response status and detail, then adds links for related operations such as finalize, authorization, orders, and certificate retrieval. GetLocation retrieves a resource URL; UpdateAccount and Deactivate run the corresponding account commands. Right-click rows in the command, authorization, challenge, or order lists for supported row actions. Notes ACME requires a reachable directory endpoint, valid account credentials, fresh replay nonces, and successful domain authorization. Keep the ACME account private key confidential. Changing account keys or deactivating an account affects the server-side ACME account. Review the server response and HTTP status after every operation. A successful request submission does not mean domain authorization or certificate issuance succeeded. Challenge validation may require DNS or web-server configuration outside BerEditor. Complete that step before finalizing the order.

docs.text: BER Format Check Dialog Guide The BER format check dialog checks whether BER-encoded data matches a supported PKI format. It can identify a format, validate a selected format, open format-specific details, or decode the data in the main BerEditor window. Open it from Tool > Check BER . Figure 1. BER format check dialog. Provide a file or encoded source, identify or select a format, then choose the appropriate check or view action. Supported Formats The dialog can identify or check these formats: Certificate CRL (certificate revocation list) CSR (certificate signing request) PublicKey PrivateKey PrivateKeyInfo EncPrivateKey (encrypted private key) CMS PKCS7 OCSP response CMP message Screen Areas Format list — Shows the formats supported by the checker. BER file — Select this to use a file as the source. The Find button opens a BER file picker, and the path is shown beside the checkbox. Source format — When BER file is unchecked, choose how the source text is represented: Hex or Base64 . Source length — Shows the calculated length for the selected source representation. Source input — Enter or paste the encoded bytes when using text input. BER Type Check — Detects the source's supported PKI format and selects it in the format list. Format selector — Choose a specific format to validate or inspect. Format Check — Checks whether the source conforms to the selected format and reports success or an error. V — Opens the format-specific information view after validating the selected format. Encrypted private keys require a password. D — Decodes the source in the main BerEditor window using the selected format title. Clear — Clears the file path and source text. Close — Closes the dialog. Check a Source File or Value Choose the source method: To check a file, select BER file , then select Find and choose the file. To check encoded text, leave BER file unchecked, select Hex or Base64 , and enter the source in the input area. Select BER Type Check to detect a supported format, or choose the expected format from the format selector. Select Format Check to validate the source against the selected format. Read the success message or the reported format error. Open Details or Decode After choosing a format, select V to open its detail window. The selected format must pass its format check. Available detail views include certificate, CRL, CSR, public/private key, CMS/PKCS7, OCSP response, and CMP message information. Select D to decode the source in the main BER view. A format must be selected first. For an encrypted private key, V prompts for the password before showing key details. Notes and Troubleshooting When using text input, the source must match its selected representation ( Hex or Base64 ). Invalid or empty input cannot be checked. BER Type Check identifies only the formats listed above. If the source is unsupported or malformed, the dialog reports that it could not determine a supported format. Format Check requires a format selection. Choose the expected type or run BER Type Check first. Use Clear before starting a new check to remove the previous file path and source text.

docs.text: BER Compare Dialog Guide The BER Compare dialog compares two BER files by their encoded bytes and decoded tree structure. Open it from Tool > BER Compare . Figure 1. BER Compare dialog. Load one file into each side, then compare the structures and inspect matched values. Screen Areas SET order support — Enables matching of SET children without relying on their position in the tree. Use this when the order of SET elements should not affect matching. A File / B File — Shows the selected file path for each side. Find — Selects a BER file for side A or B and loads its decoded tree. D — Decodes the corresponding file in BerEditor's main window. A BER Information / B BER Information — Displays the decoded BER tree for each file. Selecting a node highlights it and its corresponding node on the other side when a match is found. BER A and B value — Shows the selected nodes' headers and values side by side. If hidden, select Show Value to display this pane. Status / Compare — Select Compare to compare the loaded BER data. The status reports whether A and B are the same or different. Clear — Clears both file paths, trees, and value panes. Show Value — Shows the BER A and B value pane. Close — Closes the dialog. Compare Two BER Files Select Find on the A File row and choose the first BER file. Select Find on the B File row and choose the second BER file. Optionally enable SET order support if SET elements may appear in a different order. Select Compare . Read the status message. Matching tree nodes are highlighted; select a node to inspect its corresponding node and value on the other side. You can also drag and drop two local files onto the dialog. The first file fills A and the second fills B. If both sides are already populated, clear the dialog before dropping different files. Inspect or Decode a File Select a node in either tree to display its encoded header and value in the comparison pane. Select D beside a file path to decode that file in the main BerEditor window. If the value pane is not visible, select Show Value . Select Clear before starting another comparison. How Results Are Determined The dialog first checks whether the complete BER byte sequences are identical. For differing files, it compares nodes by tag, tree depth, definite/indefinite length form, length, and value. A difference in any of these makes the corresponding nodes different. With SET order support enabled, SET children are matched by their parent path rather than their original position. Both files must be loaded before comparison. If either side is empty, BerEditor asks you to select that file.

docs.text: Binary View Dialog Guide The Binary View dialog displays binary data as Base64, a formatted hexadecimal dump, or a continuous hexadecimal value. Open it from Tool > Binary View . Figure 1. Binary View dialog. Base64 is selected by default; use Find to load a file and change the output format as needed. The implementation file is named bin_view_dlg , while the menu and dialog call this feature Binary View . Screen Areas Find — Opens a file picker and loads a binary file for viewing. Base64 — Displays the data as Base64 text. This is the default format. Hex — Displays a hexadecimal dump in rows of up to 16 bytes. Raw — Displays the complete hexadecimal value without row formatting. Address — In Hex view, includes each row's offset. Available only in Hex view. ASCII — In Hex view, adds printable characters beside each row. Available only in Hex view. PEM — Wraps Base64 output with BEGIN and END lines. Available only in Base64 view. PEM type — Selects or enters the label used in the PEM header and footer. The list includes common key, certificate, CSR, CRL, PKCS#7/CMS, and parameter labels. Output area — Shows the selected representation. It is read-only. Print / Print Preview — Prints the displayed output or previews it before printing. Close — Closes the dialog. View Binary Data Select Find and choose a file, or open Binary View from a selected value in BerEditor. Choose Base64 , Hex , or Raw . For Hex view, optionally enable Address and ASCII . For Base64 view, optionally enable PEM and choose or enter a PEM type. Use Print or Print Preview if you need a paper copy. Display updates automatically when the format or its options change. The data area is read-only. A local file can also be dragged onto the dialog to load it. Format Details Base64 output is line-wrapped. With PEM enabled, the selected label is used in the PEM boundary lines. Hex output is grouped into 16-byte rows. Address shows the offset, and ASCII shows printable characters for each row. Raw output is a continuous hexadecimal string; Address and ASCII options are unavailable.

docs.text: BN Calculator Dialog Guide The BN Calculator performs arbitrary-precision integer and finite-field calculations. Choose a numeric representation and a base group, enter values in A , B , and, when needed, M , then select an operation. Figure 1. BN Calculator with Hex input and the Number base group selected. Available operations depend on the selected base group. Screen Areas Numeric type — Choose Binary , Decimal , or Hex . The same representation is used to read inputs and display results. Only digits valid for the selected base are accepted. Base Group — Choose Number , Modular , or GF2m . This determines which arithmetic operations are available and how the optional M value is used. A, B, and M fields — Enter operands. M is the modulus used by modular operations; it is disabled when the selected group does not need it. Each section shows the input length and provides its own controls. C, +1, and -1 — Clear a value or increment/decrement it by one. Bits, GenPrime, and IsPrime — Choose a bit length and generate a prime for A , B , or M . IsPrime tests the value in that section. Available bit sizes range from 8 to 4096. Copy / Paste — Copy a value to the clipboard or paste clipboard contents into the field. Result — Displays the calculation result in the selected numeric type. Send to A , Send to B , and Send to M copy the result into the corresponding operand. Copy copies the result; C clears it. Timer / Calculation / Sum — Shows the most recent operation and elapsed time in milliseconds. Auto sum adds each operation time to the running total; Add and Sub manually adjust the total. The adjacent C buttons clear the individual time or sum. Operation buttons — Run arithmetic, modular, bitwise, shift, or number-theory operations. The available buttons and labels vary with Base Group . Clear All / Close — Clear all operand and result values, or close the dialog. Base Groups and Operations Base Group Operations and behavior Number Standard integer addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, square, remainder, GCD, bitwise OR/AND/XOR/complement, shifts, and prime checks. The modular operand is not used. Modular Arithmetic modulo M , including modular addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, square, shift, inverse, and square root. Operations that require an inverse or square root may fail if the mathematical conditions are not met. GF2m Arithmetic in a binary extension field using the selected field modulus M . Available operations include field addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, square, remainder, inverse, square root, and shifts as enabled in the dialog. Perform a Calculation Select a Numeric type and Base Group . Enter the required operand values. Use A and B for binary operations; provide M when the selected operation is modular or uses a GF2m modulus. Select the operation button. The result appears in Result , and the operation time is shown in Timer . To continue calculating, use Send to A , Send to B , or Send to M to reuse the result as an operand. Generate or Check a Prime In the desired operand section, choose a bit size from Bits . Select GenPrime to generate a prime and place it in that field. To test a value already entered, select IsPrime . The result is reported in BerEditor's message/log area. Timing Operations Timer displays the latest operation and its elapsed time. Enable Auto sum to add each measured operation time to Sum automatically. Use Add or Sub to adjust the sum by the latest operation time. Clear the latest timer or accumulated sum with its adjacent C button. Notes Hexadecimal values with an odd number of digits are padded with a leading zero internally for input conversion. Division by zero, invalid modular inverses, and other undefined operations produce a calculation error. In Modular and GF2m groups, select a valid modulus M appropriate to the operation. A generated prime can help create a modulus for prime-field calculations. The GF2m group performs arithmetic over a binary extension field; its operations do not use ordinary integer arithmetic semantics.

docs.text: CertMan Dialog Guide The Certificate Management dialog organizes certificates, private keys, certificate authorities, CRLs, and trusted root CAs. It also provides common certificate and key operations. The available tabs and actions depend on the selected management mode. Figure 1. CertMan on the End Entity tab. Select a certificate row to view, export, verify, or use its associated key. Tabs End Entity — Manage end-entity certificates and their associated private keys. The table shows subject DN, expiration, and issuer DN. Use the password field when the stored private key is encrypted. Other Cert — Manage additional certificates that are not in the End Entity list; inspect, decode, verify, encrypt to, export, add, or remove them. CA — Manage CA certificates used to build certificate paths. Add, view, decode, export, or remove CA certificates. CRL — Manage certificate revocation lists. Add, view, decode, export, or remove CRLs. Trust RootCA — Manage trusted root certificates, view or export their public keys, load system trust certificates, and remove trust entries. Tools — Work with a private key, certificate, or PFX file. Check key-pair correspondence, inspect key/certificate data, create or extract a PFX, encrypt/decrypt a PFX, and save a PFX entry into End Entity storage. End Entity Screen Areas Certificate Path — Shows the configured End Entity certificate storage folder. The filter can show all entries or narrow the list by key algorithm. Certificate table — Lists stored end-entity certificates by subject DN, expiration date, and issuer DN. Select a row before using the action buttons. Password — Enter the password for an encrypted private key associated with the selected certificate when a private-key action requires it. View Cert / View PriKey / View PubKey — Inspect the selected certificate or its associated private/public key. Decode Cert / Decode PriKey / Decode PriKey Info — Decode certificate, private-key, or private-key information data in BerEditor. Check KeyPair — Check whether the selected certificate's public key matches its associated private key. Run Sign / Run Verify / Run Encrypt / Run Decrypt — Launch the corresponding cryptographic operation using the selected certificate/key material. Change Passwd — Change the password protecting the selected private key. Import PFX / Export PFX — Import or export a PFX package containing certificate/key material. Delete Cert — Remove the selected end-entity entry. OK / Close — OK confirms a selection when CertMan is opened in a selection mode. Close dismisses the dialog. docs.text: Certificate Path Validation Dialog Guide The Certificate Path Validation dialog helps build and inspect a certificate chain, validate a target certificate, check certificate policies, and verify CRLs. It can use certificates and CRLs selected from files or stored in BerEditor's CertMan lists. Figure 1. Certificate Path Validation dialog. Supply trust and revocation data, select a target certificate, then build or validate its certificate path. Screen Areas Use TrustList / Trust List — Enable Use TrustList to validate against BerEditor's configured trust list. Trust List opens CertMan's root CA list. When disabled, provide a specific TrustCert file for the operation. TrustCert, UntrustCert, and CRL — Select files with Find or choose entries from CertMan with Add . V opens certificate or CRL information; D decodes the selected file in BerEditor. TrustCert supplies trust anchors, UntrustCert supplies certificates treated as untrusted, and CRL supplies revocation information. Include CertMan CA in UntrustCert — Includes CertMan CA certificates in the untrusted certificate input for path validation. Path Clear / VerifyCRL / VerifyCert — Path Clear clears the displayed path. VerifyCRL checks a CRL against the selected trust or untrusted certificate. VerifyCert checks the selected certificate using the trust, untrusted, and optional CRL inputs. At Time / Make Path / Clear — Enable At Time to use the selected date and time for path checks. Make Path builds a chain for the target certificate; Clear clears the path list and tree. Path List / Path Tree — View the built chain as a table or hierarchical tree. Double-click an entry to view its details. Right-click for available item actions. Flag Options — Configure certificate-path verification behavior, including CRL checking, policy checks, critical-extension handling, strict X.509 processing, time checks, partial chains, and trust-anchor selection. Use flags only when their validation behavior is intended. Param — Add verification parameters such as Policy , Purpose , Name , Depth , AuthLevel , HostName , Email , and IP , with a corresponding value. Add appends the selected parameter; Clear removes the parameter list. Right-click table entries for item actions. Certificate target — Select the target certificate with Find or L (select from CertMan). The subject DN appears in the adjacent field. V views certificate details and D decodes it in BerEditor. Policy Check / Path Validation — Run a policy check or validate the target's certificate path using the selected inputs, flags, parameters, and time options. Include CertMan CRL in CRL adds CertMan CRLs to path validation. Clear Data All / Close — Clear the dialog's inputs and results or close the dialog. Build a Certificate Path Select a target certificate using Find or L . The subject DN confirms the selected target. Enable Use TrustList to use the configured trust list, or select a TrustCert file for a specific trust anchor. Add any relevant UntrustCert certificates and CRL data. To use CertMan's stored CA or CRL data, enable the applicable inclusion option. If required, enable At Time and set the validation date and time. Configure any needed verification flags and parameters. Select Make Path . Review the resulting chain in Path List or Path Tree . When online CA/CRL retrieval is enabled in BerEditor settings, path construction may retrieve issuer or status data online. Validate a Certificate or Check a CRL To check the target certificate, select the certificate and configure the trust and revocation inputs, then select VerifyCert . Review the result reported in the log. To verify a CRL, provide a CRL and its issuing certificate as TrustCert or UntrustCert, then select VerifyCRL . To perform full path validation, select Path Validation after setting the target, trust data, optional CRLs, flags, parameters, and time. Use Policy Check when you want to check the configured certificate policy parameters. Verification Flags The dialog exposes these options (some may be below the visible area depending on window size): Option Use UseCheckTime / NoCheckTime / At Time Control certificate time evaluation and the selected validation time. CRLCheck / CRLCheckAll Enable CRL checking for certificates in the chain or throughout the chain. IgnoreCritical Ignore unrecognized critical extensions. X509Strict Apply stricter X.509 checks. PolicyCheck / ExplicitPolicy Enable policy processing and explicit policy requirements. InhibitAny / InhibitMap Restrict anyPolicy or policy mapping behavior. PartialChain Allow a chain to terminate at an intermediate certificate. TrustedFirst Prefer trusted certificates when building the chain. Notes A successful path depends on a valid target certificate, suitable trust anchors, complete issuer certificates, and any required revocation data. VerifyCert , VerifyCRL , Policy Check , and Path Validation are separate operations and report their results in BerEditor's message/log area. Online retrieval during Make Path follows the online CA/CRL setting configured in BerEditor.

docs.text: Encrypt / Decrypt Dialog Guide The Encrypt / Decrypt dialog performs symmetric encryption or decryption on entered data or a file. Open it from Cryptography > Encrypt/Decrypt . Figure 1. Encrypt / Decrypt dialog. This view shows input data mode, the AEAD section, and cipher settings. Screen Areas Input Data / Input File — Enter data directly or select a file to process. Source data — Choose the input representation and enter or paste data. The Len field reports the decoded length. In file mode, use Find to select the source file and review its size and progress. Init / Update / Final / Reset — Run the operation incrementally: initialize the cipher, process data blocks with Update, finish with Final, or reset the state. Key — Select the key representation and enter a key, or leave it blank to choose a symmetric key from Key List. The length is shown beside the field. IV — Select the IV representation and enter the initialization vector. The note in the dialog describes IV requirements for the selected mode. AEAD — Enables authenticated encryption modes and associated data controls. Select AAD and enter additional authenticated data. The tag length, tag value, and CCM data length controls are used by the selected AEAD mode. Encrypt / Decrypt — Choose the operation. The result field is labeled Encrypted data or Decrypted data accordingly. Algorithm / Mode — Select a symmetric cipher and mode. Available modes depend on whether AEAD is selected and on the chosen algorithm. Padding — Enables padding where supported by the selected algorithm and mode. Encrypt / Decrypt button — Runs the selected operation on the current text or file. Result — Displays the output in the selected representation. The length updates automatically. The up-arrow transfers the output into the input field and selects the matching representation. Clear Data All / Close — Clears the dialog's data or closes the dialog. Encrypt or Decrypt Text Select Input Data and choose the source data format. Enter or paste the plaintext (for encryption) or ciphertext (for decryption). Enter the key and IV, or select a key from Key List when prompted. Choose Encrypt or Decrypt , then select the algorithm and mode. For AEAD modes, enable AEAD , provide AAD if required, and set the tag parameters. For CCM, provide the data length requested by the dialog. Select Encrypt or Decrypt to run the operation. Review the result. Use the output format selector to view the result as Hex, String, or Base64. Process a File Select Input File , then select Find and choose a source file. Select or enter a destination file path using the destination-file controls. Set the key, IV, operation, algorithm, and mode. Configure AEAD options if applicable. Select Encrypt or Decrypt and monitor progress. Supported Modes and Notes Standard modes include CBC , ECB , CTR , CFB , and OFB . When AEAD is enabled, the available authenticated modes include GCM and CCM . ChaCha20 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 have mode and padding controls constrained by the cipher implementation. For AEAD decryption, provide the authentication tag associated with the ciphertext. Authentication failure prevents successful decryption. The input and output fields support Hex, String, and Base64 representations. Ensure the selected representation matches the text entered. Incremental Processing For staged input, select Init , enter a block and select Update for each block, then select Final . The status fields show progress. Select Reset before starting a new operation.

docs.text: EST Client Dialog Guide The EST Client communicates with an Enrollment over Secure Transport (EST) server to retrieve CA certificates and prepare certificate enrollment requests. Figure 1. docs.text: Hash Dialog Guide The Hash dialog calculates a digest for text or a file. Open it from Cryptography > Hash . Figure 1. Hash dialog on the Input Data tab. Select a source, choose a hash algorithm, and select Digest to calculate the digest. Screen Areas Input Data / Input File — Choose whether to enter data directly or hash a file. Input Type — Select how the input text is represented (for example, Hex, String, or Base64). Input area / Input File controls — Enter text in Input Data, or select Find in Input File to choose a file. File mode displays file information, total and read sizes, and progress. Init / Update / Final — Run a hash incrementally: initialize the selected algorithm, add the current input to the hash state, then finalize and display the digest. Reset clears the incremental operation status. Status — Shows the state of the incremental operation. Algorithm — Select the hash algorithm. The list is provided by the application and may depend on the build and crypto configuration. Request length — Sets the output length for SHAKE128 or SHAKE256. It is disabled for fixed-length hash algorithms. The default is 32 bytes. Digest — Calculates a one-shot digest for the selected input data or file. Digest Value — Displays the digest in hexadecimal. Its Len field shows the output length. C clears the digest. Clear Data All — Clears input, output, and status fields. Close — Closes the dialog. Calculate a Digest from Text Select Input Data . Choose the Input Type and enter or paste the data. Select a hash Algorithm . For SHAKE128 or SHAKE256, enter the desired Request length in bytes. Select Digest . The digest appears in hexadecimal in Digest Value . Calculate a Digest from a File Select Input File . Select Find and choose a file. Review the file information and select the threading option if shown. Select Digest and wait for the progress indicator to complete. The dialog reads the file in blocks and updates the read size and progress. Large files can be processed without loading the entire file into the input text area. Incremental Hashing Use Init , Update , and Final when you want to feed data to the hash operation in stages: Select an algorithm and choose Init . Enter a data block and select Update . Repeat for additional blocks. Select Final to calculate and display the digest. Select Reset to clear the operation state before starting another sequence. Notes The input length and digest length are displayed automatically. Use the same algorithm and input bytes when reproducing or comparing a digest. An empty input is allowed for one-shot digest calculation; it produces the digest of the empty byte sequence.

docs.text: OTP Generator Dialog Guide The OTP Generator creates a time-based one-time password (OTP) from a symmetric key, a selected time, a hash algorithm, and a time interval. Figure 1. OTP Generator dialog. Set the timestamp and OTP parameters, provide the shared key, then generate the code. Screen Areas Date and Time — Select the timestamp used for generation. Set now fills in the current local time. Epoch — Shows the selected date and time as Unix time in seconds. It updates when the date/time changes. Hash — Select the hash algorithm used to generate the OTP. The initial selection follows BerEditor's configured default hash. Interval — Set the time-step duration in seconds. The default is 60 seconds. Length — Set the number of decimal digits in the OTP. The default is 6 digits. Key properties — Select the key representation ( Hex , String , or Base64 ) and enter the shared secret key. The adjacent field shows its length. If the key field is empty when generating, the dialog opens KeyList so you can select a symmetric key. T value — Displays the time-step value used for this generation, in hexadecimal. OTP — Displays the generated password as decimal digits. Gen OTP / Clear Data All / Close — Generate the OTP, clear the key and result fields, or close the dialog. Generate an OTP Set Date and Time , or select Set now to use the current time. Confirm the corresponding Epoch value. Choose the Hash , Interval , and OTP Length expected by the other system or authenticator. Enter the shared secret in Key properties and choose its representation. If left blank, select a key from KeyList when prompted. Select Gen OTP . The time-step value and decimal OTP appear in their result fields. Notes OTP verification requires matching parameters on both sides, including the shared secret, hash, time interval, and code length. Clock differences can cause a code to be rejected. The generated OTP is associated with the selected timestamp and interval; use Set now when generating a code for the current time. Treat the shared key as sensitive. The generation details, including the key and OTP, are also written to BerEditor's log. Clear Data All clears the key and result values. It does not change the selected time or OTP parameters.

docs.text: Get BER from URI Dialog Guide The Get BER from URI dialog retrieves BER-encoded data from an HTTP(S) or LDAP address and loads the result into the main BerEditor window for decoding. Open it from Tool > Get BER from URI . Figure 1. Get BER from URI dialog. Enter an HTTP(S) or LDAP address, or enable LDAP Host Information to supply LDAP connection and search details separately. Screen Areas URI Address — Enter or select an address. Recent addresses are available from the drop-down list. The dialog accepts http , https , and ldap schemes. Example — Shows an example certificate URL. Clear Used URI — Removes the saved recent URI list. Use LDAP Host Information — Switches from a full URI to separately entered LDAP connection details. When enabled, the URI field is disabled and the LDAP Host Information group is enabled. LDAP Host Information — Enter the LDAP server Host , Port , and search DN . The host and port are retained as settings for later use. LDAP Search Condition — Supplies LDAP search options: Scope , certificate Type , and Filter . The default filter is (objectClass=*) . Get — Retrieves data from the selected address and asks BerEditor to decode the returned data. Close — Closes the dialog. Retrieve Data from an HTTP(S) URI Leave Use LDAP Host Information unchecked. Enter or select an http:// or https:// address in URI Address . Select Get . If retrieval succeeds, BerEditor decodes the returned data in the main window and displays a success message. The address can also be selected from the recent URI list. Successfully used addresses are saved in that list. Clear Used URI removes the saved list. Retrieve Data from LDAP You can provide LDAP details in either of these ways: Use an LDAP URI Leave Use LDAP Host Information unchecked. Enter an ldap:// URI that identifies the LDAP server and search location. Set the search Type and Filter if needed. Select Get . The dialog reads the server, DN, scope, filter, and requested attribute from the LDAP URI when those values are present. The selected Type and filter field are used as defaults where the URI does not specify them. Enter LDAP Host Information Separately Select Use LDAP Host Information . Enter the LDAP server Host , Port , and DN . Choose a Scope , Type , and Filter . Select Get . The current implementation provides the BASE scope. Available certificate types are caCertificate , signCertificate , userCertificate , certificateRevocationList , autorithRevocationList , deltaRevocationList , and certificateTrustList . Troubleshooting Enter an address before selecting Get . The dialog reports an error when the URI is empty or uses an unsupported scheme. For LDAP host mode, provide a DN. Check the host, port, and server availability if connection or bind errors appear. If retrieval fails, BerEditor reports the retrieval error in a warning or log message. Retrieved data is passed to the main BER decoder. If the server returns data that is not valid BER, decoding may fail even when the network request succeeds.

docs.text: Key Agreement Dialog Guide The Key Agreement dialog calculates a shared secret using Diffie–Hellman (DH) or Elliptic Curve Diffie–Hellman (ECDH). It can also generate the parameters and key material used in the calculation. Figure 1. Key Agreement dialog with the DH tab selected. The ECDH tab provides equivalent key agreement controls for elliptic-curve keys. Screen Areas DH / ECDH tabs — Select finite-field DH or elliptic-curve ECDH. DH parameters — In the DH tab, choose Parameter Len , select the g value (generator), and enter the p value (prime modulus) as hexadecimal. GenParam generates DH parameters. Import and Export load and save DH parameters. A and B keys — Enter each participant's private and public keys in hexadecimal. Use GenPriKey to generate a private key and GenKeyPair to generate a key pair. The public key is derived from the corresponding private key and DH/ECDH parameters. ECDH parameters and key tools — In the ECDH tab, choose a curve or parameter set. The adjacent field displays its identifier. The A and B key areas provide controls to generate or check keys, find a private-key file, or retrieve keys from CertMan or KeyPairMan. Edit Mode — Enables editing of all A/B private and public key fields. In calculation mode, only the fields needed for the selected participant are enabled. A Calculate / B Calculate — Select which participant computes the shared secret. Run performs that calculation. Display shared key Y value — For ECDH, also display the Y component of the computed shared point when available. The shared secret's X component is shown by default. Secret Key — Displays the calculated result in hexadecimal and its length. C clears this output. Clear Data All / Close — Clear the dialog's values or close the dialog. Calculate a DH Shared Secret Select the DH tab. Choose a parameter length and generator, or enter/import the agreed p and g values. Both participants must use the same parameters. Enter or generate A's and B's private/public keys. For A's calculation, provide A PrivateKey and B PublicKey . For B's calculation, provide B PrivateKey and A PublicKey . Select A Calculate or B Calculate , then select Run . Read the resulting shared value in Secret Key . The dialog also writes calculation details to BerEditor's log. Calculate an ECDH Shared Secret Select the ECDH tab and choose the same curve or parameter set used by both participants. Enter or generate the participant key pairs. To calculate as A, provide A PrivateKey and B PublicKey ; to calculate as B, provide B PrivateKey and A PublicKey . Select the calculation side and choose Run . Read the shared secret in Secret Key . Enable Display shared key Y value if you also need the Y component shown. Generate and Import Parameters or Keys In the DH tab, select a parameter length and use GenParam to create parameters. Use Export to save them or Import to load existing parameters. Use GenPriKey and GenKeyPair to create DH key material. The private key and public key must belong to the same participant and parameters. In the ECDH tab, select the desired curve before generating keys. The FindPriKey , GetFromCertMan , and GetFromKeyPair controls can load existing private/public key material. The check controls validate the displayed public key or key pair. Notes A and B must use the same DH parameters or ECDH curve, and each side must calculate with its own private key and the other side's public key. Both calculations should produce the same shared secret. Values entered directly in the key and parameter fields use hexadecimal encoding. Edit Mode is useful when preparing both participants' values manually; the normal A/B calculation selection enables the inputs required for that calculation. Treat private keys and shared secrets as sensitive data. Clear the fields when finished if the dialog should not retain them.

docs.text: KeyList Dialog Guide The Symmetric Key List dialog stores and selects symmetric keys used by BerEditor's encryption, decryption, and MAC tools. The list displays each key's name, algorithm, length, IV availability, and last-modified time. Figure 1. Key List in management mode. Select a row to view, delete, or use the stored key. Screen Areas Save Path — Shows the configured key-list storage folder. The adjacent filter shows All keys or narrows the list by algorithm, including generic keys and HMAC keys. Key table — Lists stored keys with Name , Algorithm , Len , IV , and LastModified columns. IV indicates whether an initialization vector is associated with the entry. Select a row before using an action. Key View — Opens the selected key entry for inspection. Key Add — Opens the key editor to create a named key entry. Enter its algorithm, key value, and optional IV. Key Delete — Removes the selected key entry from the configured key-list folder. Gen MAC — Opens the MAC generator using the selected key. Encrypt/Decrypt — Opens the symmetric encryption/decryption tool using the selected key. OK / Close — In selection mode, OK returns the selected key (and associated IV where applicable) to the calling dialog. Close dismisses the key list. Add or Inspect a Key Select Key Add and enter a unique key name, algorithm, key value, and optional IV in the key editor. Save the entry. It appears in the table with its algorithm, length, IV indicator, and modification time. Select a row and choose Key View to inspect the stored entry. In management mode, right-click a row for the view and delete actions. Select a Key for Another Tool Open KeyList from the dialog that needs a symmetric key. Optionally filter by algorithm, then select the desired key row. Select OK or double-click the row to return the key to the calling dialog. Notes A key entry's name must be unique within the configured key-list folder. The key list supports algorithm-specific and generic key entries, as well as HMAC keys. The caller may filter the list to a specific algorithm. Treat stored symmetric keys and IV values as sensitive. Deleting an entry removes its file from the key-list folder.

docs.text: Key Management Dialog Guide The Key Management dialog provides three tools: key derivation, symmetric key wrapping/unwrapping, and key encapsulation. Open it from Cryptography > Key Manage . Figure 1. Key Management dialog on the KeyDerive tab. The dialog also contains KeyWrap and KEM tabs. Tabs Tab Purpose KeyDerive Derives a key using PBKDF2, HKDF, ANS X9.63, or Scrypt. KeyWrap Wraps or unwraps key bytes using KW or KWP and a key-encryption key (KEK). KEM Encapsulates a shared key using a public key or decapsulates it using the matching private key. Key Derivation Open KeyDerive and select a derivation method. Enter the password or secret and choose its input representation where available. Enter method-specific salt and information values, and select a hash where applicable. Set the desired Derived Key Len in bytes and any method parameters. Select Derive Key . The derived key is displayed as hexadecimal. Method Main inputs PBKDF2 Password (String), salt, iteration count, hash, and key length. HKDF Secret, salt, optional Info, hash, and key length. A salt is required by this dialog. ANS.X963 Secret, Info, hash, and key length. Scrypt Password, salt, N/r/p parameters, and key length. The hash and Info controls are not used. The input type selectors for secret, salt, and Info use the available data formats shown by the dialog, such as Hex, String, and Base64. Length fields are calculated automatically. Use the salt C button or the derived-key C button to clear those fields. Clear Data All clears the dialog's derivation, wrapping, and KEM data. Key Wrap and Unwrap Open KeyWrap and choose KW or KWP under Method . Choose Wrap or Unwrap . Enter the source key (for Wrap) or wrapped key (for Unwrap). Select the input representation. Enter the KEK and its representation, or use Gen KEK to generate an AES key of the selected length (16, 24, or 32 bytes). Select Run . The result is shown in hexadecimal. In Wrap mode, the result is the Wrapped Key . In Unwrap mode, the result is the recovered Source key . The up-arrow button moves the result into the source field for another operation. In KW mode, the source key must be at least 16 bytes. KWP supports padding for inputs that do not meet the KW block-size requirement. Key Encapsulation (KEM) KEM uses a public key to generate a shared key and an encapsulated value, then uses the matching private key to recover the same shared key. Encapsulate Open KEM and select Encapsulate . Choose the public key source: select Use CertMan to select from certificate management, or enable Select private key or public key and provide a certificate or public key file. Select Encapsulate . The generated shared key and wrapped/encapsulated key are shown as hexadecimal values. Decapsulate Select Decapsulate . Choose the private key source: Use CertMan , or enable Select private key or public key and provide a private key file. If the private key file is encrypted, select its encrypted-key option and enter the password. Enter the encapsulated value in Wrapped Key and select Decapsulate . The recovered shared key appears in the key output field. The KEM operation supports RSA, ECDSA, and ML-KEM key types in the current implementation. The key and encapsulated-value fields provide Find , View , Decode , or Type actions for the selected file, where available. Clear buttons remove the corresponding values. Troubleshooting Check that the selected representation matches the entered text. Invalid Hex or Base64 input prevents the operation. Key derivation requires a password or secret. HKDF also requires a salt. Key wrapping requires both source data and a KEK. KW requires a source key of at least 16 bytes. KEM encapsulation requires a supported public key or certificate; decapsulation requires the matching supported private key and encapsulated value. Operation failures are reported in a warning, and activity details may also appear in the BerEditor log.

docs.text: KeyPairMan Dialog Guide The Key Pair Management dialog stores, selects, inspects, and uses asymmetric key pairs in BerEditor's KeyPairMan. A key pair is shown with its algorithm, parameter set, and modification time. Figure 1. KeyPairMan on the List tab. Select a key-pair row to perform an action on that key. Screen Areas List / Tools tabs — List manages stored key pairs. Tools works with private keys, public keys, encrypted private keys, private-key information, and certificate signing requests (CSRs). KeyPair Path — Shows the configured KeyPairMan storage folder. The adjacent filter limits listed key pairs by algorithm or shows All . Key-pair table — Lists stored pairs by folder name, algorithm, option/parameter, and last-modified time. Select a row before using the action buttons. Gen KeyPair / Import — Generate a new pair or import key material into KeyPairMan. View PubKey / View PriKey — Inspect the selected pair's public or private key. Private key material is sensitive. Decode PubKey / Decode PriKey — Decode the selected key in BerEditor's main window. Run Encrypt / Run Decrypt / Run Sign / Run Verify — Open the corresponding operation using the selected key material. Make CSR — Create a certificate signing request using the selected key pair. Export / Delete / Rename — Export the selected pair, remove it from KeyPairMan, or change its name. Tools tab controls — Load private/public key files, inspect or decode them, check that a pair matches, create a CSR, save a pair to the list, and encrypt/decrypt a private key. The private-key encryption mode and password are set in this tab. Save as DER — Select DER output for supported export/save operations in the Tools tab. OK / Close — OK confirms selection when the dialog is being used to choose a key pair. Close dismisses the manager. Manage Key Pairs Open the List tab and select a row, or choose Gen KeyPair or Import to add key material. Use View , Decode , or Make CSR to inspect or prepare the selected pair. Use the Run buttons to launch encryption, decryption, signing, or verification with the selected key. Use Export , Rename , or Delete as needed. Deleting removes the stored key-pair entry from KeyPairMan. Use the Tools Tab Open Tools and use Find beside the private-key or public-key field to select files. The V , D , and T controls view, decode, or identify key data where available. Select Check KeyPair to confirm the public and private keys correspond. Select Make CSR to create a request from the key pair, then inspect or decode the CSR as needed. Select Save to List to add the pair to KeyPairMan. To protect or unlock a private key, provide an encrypted private-key file or key, choose an encryption mode and password, then use Encrypt PrivateKey or Decrypt PrivateKey . Notes The dialog displays a notice that private keys in KeyPairMan are not encrypted for testing purposes. Protect the storage directory and exported key files accordingly. Run operations require a compatible key type and the appropriate public or private key component. docs.text: Make BER Dialog Guide The Make BER dialog builds a BER-encoded value from a tag and value. Open it from Tool > Make BER . Figure 1. Make BER dialog. The header and BER output are updated as the tag settings and value change. Screen Areas More Type — Adds additional universal tag types to the Tag type list. Class — Selects the BER tag class: Universal , Application , Content-Specific , or Private . Constructed — Sets the constructed bit. SEQUENCE and SET are always constructed; other universal types cannot be changed to constructed in this dialog. Indefinite — Uses indefinite length for constructed data. This option is enabled only when Constructed is selected. The generated BER ends with the end-of-contents marker 00 00 . Tag / Number — For the Universal class, select a tag type from the list. For the other classes, enter the tag number in hexadecimal. The tag number for Content-Specific is limited to 1F (31) or less in this dialog. Tag bits — Shows the BER tag byte in binary ( [T] 0b ). L — Shows the generated length field in hexadecimal. Value format and input — Select the input representation and enter the value. Available formats are Hex , String , and Base64 . The Len field shows the decoded value length. C — Clears the value input. Make Value — Opens a helper for supported value types such as BitString, Integer, or ObjectIdentifier. Availability depends on the selected tag and value format. BER Header — Displays the generated tag and length bytes in hexadecimal. BER output — Displays the complete BER value in hexadecimal. Its Len field shows the output length. Make — Validates and accepts the generated BER value. From Tool > Make BER , the value is then loaded into the main BER view. Close — Closes the dialog without accepting the generated value. Create a BER Value Open Tool > Make BER . Choose a Class . For Universal , choose a tag type. Use More Type if the required universal type is not in the initial list. For another class, enter the tag Number in hexadecimal. Set Constructed or Indefinite if applicable. These controls are constrained by the selected tag class and type. Select the value format, then enter the value. The BER Header and BER output update as you edit the settings. Review the header, length, and complete BER output. Select Make to validate and load the result into the main BER view. Tag and Value Notes The default universal tag is SEQUENCE , with Constructed enabled. NULL has no value input; the value field is disabled for this tag. SEQUENCE and SET require the Constructed bit. Other universal tag types are treated as primitive by this dialog. For a constructed value with Indefinite selected, the BER output uses an indefinite length and appends 00 00 as the end-of-contents marker. A BER BOOLEAN value must be exactly one byte. For BIT STRING , the first value byte must be between 00 and 07 , representing the number of unused bits. For non-universal classes, enter the tag number in hexadecimal. The Content-Specific class uses a low tag number up to 1F here. If Validation Fails If the selected input format cannot be decoded, BerEditor reports a format error and returns focus to the value field. Correct the input format or value, then select Make again. Boolean and BitString values have the additional constraints listed above.

docs.text: Make Private Key Dialog Guide The Make Private Key dialog generates asymmetric key pairs and displays their components. It supports RSA, ECC, DSA, and raw-key algorithms, including EdDSA and post-quantum ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA. Figure 1. Make Private Key dialog with RSA selected. Use the algorithm tabs to view or edit the corresponding key components. Screen Areas Algorithm — Select the key algorithm: RSA, ECDSA, SM2, DSA, EdDSA, ML-KEM, ML-DSA, or SLH-DSA. The available parameter choices depend on the algorithm. Parameter — Choose the key size, curve, or algorithm parameter set. For RSA, the default size is 2048 bits. Other algorithms use their respective sizes or named parameter sets. Exponent — Set the RSA public exponent as a decimal value. The default is 65537 ; this setting applies to RSA key generation. PublicKey only — When enabled, the dialog generates or exports only public-key data and disables private-key components where applicable. RSA tab — Shows RSA public exponent E , primes P and Q , modulus N , private exponent D , CRT exponents DMP1 and DMQ1 , and coefficient IQMP . Values are hexadecimal; adjacent fields show their lengths. ECC tab — Shows the selected curve name and OID, private key, and public point coordinates PubX and PubY . DSA tab — Shows the domain parameters P , Q , and G , plus the public and private key values. Raw tab — Select the raw algorithm Name and Param set, then view the raw public and private key values. Raw algorithms include EdDSA, ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA. Make — Generates a key pair using the selected algorithm and parameters, then fills the corresponding tab with the generated components. For ECC, select the curve; for DSA and raw algorithms, select the supported size or parameter set. Leave PublicKey only unchecked when you need a complete key pair. Select Make . Select Save to KeyPairMan to store the key pair, or Export to write it in the desired format. Inspect or Export Existing Components Select the tab for the key algorithm. Enter or review the hexadecimal key components. The displayed length fields update as values change. Select Decode to open the encoded key in BerEditor's decoder, or use a check button to validate it. Select Export and choose whether to export public or private key material using PublicKey only . docs.text: OCSP Client Dialog Guide The OCSP Client creates an Online Certificate Status Protocol request, sends it to a responder, and verifies the returned response. It can include a nonce and optionally sign the request. Figure 1. OCSP Client dialog. Configure the responder and target certificate, encode or send a request, then verify the response. Screen Areas OCSP URL — Enter or select the responder URL. Previously used URLs are retained. Clear clears the URL history/input. Set OCSP URL from AIA / Set CA from AIA — Read the responder URL or issuer CA certificate from the target certificate's Authority Information Access information. CA cert — Select the issuer CA certificate. Find browses for a certificate; V , D , and T view, decode, and identify it. Certificate — Select the certificate whose status is being checked. The dialog can also obtain it from CertMan. The adjacent Find , V , D , and T controls select, view, decode, or identify the certificate. Use Sign / Use Nonce — Optionally sign the OCSP request with a signing certificate/private key and include a nonce. The signing certificate and key can be selected from CertMan or from individual files; enable Enc PrivateKey and enter its password for a protected key. The nonce value is hexadecimal. Request — Encode builds the OCSP request. Auto send sends it immediately after encoding; otherwise use Send . C clears the request and D decodes it in BerEditor. Verify Flags — Enable the flag group and select any applicable response-checking flags: NOCHAIN , NOSIGS , NOINTERN , NOCERTS , NOVERIFY , NOEXPLICIT , NOCASIGN , or NODELEGATED . Response — Displays the responder response in hexadecimal. View Response opens response details; View CertID inspects the certificate identifier; Verify validates the response. C clears the response and D decodes it. OCSP Certificate — Select the responder certificate when needed for response verification. Find , V , D , and T select or inspect it. Clear All / Close — Clear dialog data or close the client. Create and Send a Status Request Enter the OCSP URL or select Set OCSP URL from AIA after choosing a target certificate. Select the target Certificate . Provide its CA cert or use Set CA from AIA where available. Optionally enable Use Nonce and enter a hexadecimal nonce. Enable Use Sign and select signing credentials if the responder requires signed requests. Select Encode . Enable Auto send to transmit immediately, or select Send after reviewing the encoded request. The response is placed in the Response area when the HTTP request succeeds. Verify a Response Select the relevant responder certificate if needed. Configure Verify Flags according to the verification requirements. Select Verify and review the result in BerEditor's message/log area. Use View Response and View CertID to inspect details. Notes The CA certificate identifies the issuer of the certificate being checked; the OCSP responder certificate is used to verify the signed response. These may be different certificates. Request signing is optional and is separate from the responder's response signature. A successful HTTP send only confirms the responder returned data. Use Verify to validate the OCSP response before relying on its status.

docs.text: PDF Signer Dialog Guide The PDF Signer signs and verifies PDF documents, adds document security and timestamp information, builds certificate paths, and encrypts or decrypts PDF files. Figure 1. PDF Signer with the Information tab and Signature controls visible. Use the Verification and Encryption tabs for their respective operations. Screen Areas PDF Path / Find — Select the source PDF. Get PDF Information reads document metadata and signature information; C clears the displayed source information. Source PDF Information tabs — Information lists PDF properties; DSS DocTimeStamp shows document security store and document timestamp details; Path Tree displays certificate-path information. Make Path builds a path for the signing/verification certificate. Source PDF Password — Enter the password when the source PDF is encrypted. Signature tab — Set signature labels: Name , Reason , Location , ContactInfo , and Date Time . Enable Use Subject DN to use the certificate subject as the signer name. Timestamp and DSS options — Enable Use Timestamp and configure TSP to request a signature timestamp. DSS adds validation data; VRI adds per-signature validation-related information when DSS is enabled. DocTimeStamp adds a document timestamp. Sign / Compress / DSS buttons — Sign creates the PDF signature. Compress controls compression where supported. Add DSS , Add DSS VRI , and Add DocTSP add validation or timestamp data to a PDF. Verification tab — Configure certificate verification using the certificate, Trust List, CA List, and optional At Time setting. Use Verify Chain and the DSS, VRI, or document-timestamp verification controls to inspect the relevant PDF validation data. Encryption tab — Use Encrypt or Decrypt for PDF encryption operations. Provide the required passwords and destination as prompted. Destination PDF / Find / up-arrow — Choose the output PDF path. Find browses for a destination; the up-arrow copies the source path into the destination field. Clear All / Close — Clear the dialog's paths and information or close it. Sign a PDF Select a source PDF with Find and enter its password if it is encrypted. Select the signing certificate and private key through CertMan when prompted. Set the signature labels and date/time. Enable Use Subject DN if the signer name should come from the certificate. Optionally enable Use Timestamp and configure the TSP. Select DSS , VRI , or DocTimeStamp if the PDF should include validation or timestamp data. Choose a destination PDF path and select Sign . If the destination already exists, confirm whether to replace it. Verify a PDF Signature Select the signed PDF and enter its password if required. Review its signature information with Get PDF Information and inspect signer/CMS data as needed. On the Verification tab, set the certificate and trust options. Use At Time to check against a specific time. Select Verify for the signature, Verify Chain for certificate-chain validation, and the DSS/VRI or DocTSP verification commands when you need to verify embedded validation/timestamp data. Review the verification results and certificate path information. Add DSS or Document Timestamp Data Select the source PDF and build the certificate path if needed. Use Add DSS to add validation material, Add DSS VRI to add VRI-related material, or Add DocTSP to add a document timestamp. Specify the output PDF destination and inspect the updated information on the DSS DocTimeStamp tab. Encrypt or Decrypt a PDF Select the source PDF and provide its password if it is already encrypted. Open the Encryption tab and choose Encrypt or Decrypt . Provide the required credentials and destination path, then run the selected operation. A valid signature does not by itself guarantee that the signer certificate chains to a trusted authority; review signature and chain verification separately. Timestamping depends on the configured TSP service. DSS and VRI features depend on the validation information available for the signing certificate. Protect PDF passwords and signing private keys. Verification results depend on the chosen trust sources and verification time.

docs.text: PKCS7 Dialog Guide The PKCS7 dialog creates and processes PKCS#7/CMS messages. It supports data and digest containers, signing and signature verification, and enveloped-data encryption and decryption. Figure 1. PKCS7 dialog in Encode mode. Select Encode or Decode at the top; the available command and controls change with the selected mode. Screen Areas Encode / Decode — Choose whether to create a PKCS7/CMS message or process an existing one. The source and output labels change to reflect the mode. Source Data / CMS data — Enter source content or the CMS message. Choose Hex , String , or Base64 for the source representation. Read File loads a file; files can also be dragged into the dialog. In Decode mode, V , D , and T view, decode, and identify the source object. C clears the source. Select each certificate and private key — Enable this group to select certificate and private-key files directly. Find browses for a file; V , D , and T view details, decode the file in BerEditor, and show its type. Enable Encrypted PrivateKey and enter its password when the private key is password protected. PKCS7 Flags — Enable the group to apply operation flags. The available flags are NOCERTS , NOSIGS , NOCHAIN , NOINTERN , NOVERIFY , DETACHED , BINARY , and NOATTR . Their effect depends on the selected command. Verification options — In the certificate verification area, choose whether to validate At Time (using the adjacent date/time), include a selected Certificate , use the CA List , or use the Trust List . These options are used for signature verification; the default screen has Trust List enabled. Hash and cipher — Select a hash algorithm for signing-related operations and an AES-CBC cipher ( aes-128-cbc , aes-192-cbc , or aes-256-cbc ) for enveloped-data operations. Controls are enabled when relevant to the selected command. Command and Auto Detect — Choose an operation. In Decode mode, Auto Detect identifies the CMS type and dispatches to the matching decode/verify operation. Turn it off to choose a decode command manually. Run button — Executes the selected command. It is labeled Encode or Decode according to the mode. CMS data / Source data output — Displays the result and its length. The output representation selector and ⬆ transfer button let you reuse the result as input. Export saves the output. V , D , and T view, decode, and identify the output; C clears it. For encoded output, the command name is shown beside the controls. Clear Data All / Close — Clear the dialog's values or close it. Create a PKCS7/CMS Message Select Encode and enter content in Source Data , or load it with Read File . Select an encoding command: Data wraps content in a CMS Data object. Digest creates a CMS DigestedData object using the selected hash. Signed creates a signed message. Select the signing certificate and private key. Enveloped encrypts the content for the selected recipient certificate. Choose an AES-CBC cipher. Add Signed adds a signer to an existing SignedData message; choose the hash and provide the signing certificate and private key. Set any applicable flags and options. Select Encode . The CMS message appears in the output area. Use Export to save it. Decode, Verify, or Decrypt a Message Select Decode and provide the CMS data. Use Read File or drag a file into the dialog if convenient. Leave Auto Detect enabled to process supported Data, DigestedData, SignedData, or EnvelopedData according to its type. To choose explicitly, turn off Auto Detect and select Verify , Developed , GetData , or GetDigest . For Verify , configure the certificate and trust/CA/time options as needed. For Developed (decryption of EnvelopedData), select the recipient certificate and matching private key. Enter the private-key password if required. Select Decode . Extracted data, digest data, verification results, or decrypted content is shown in the output area or reported by the dialog. PKCS7 Flags Flag Purpose NOCERTS Omit signer certificates when creating signed data. NOSIGS Skip signature verification. NOCHAIN Disable certificate-chain verification. NOINTERN Do not search certificates embedded in the message. NOVERIFY Skip signer-certificate verification. DETACHED Create or process detached signed data, where content is separate from the CMS structure. BINARY Treat content as binary data. NOATTR Omit signed attributes when creating signed data. Notes The available command list depends on Encode or Decode mode. Decode Auto Detect supports CMS Data, DigestedData, SignedData, and EnvelopedData types. Signed and enveloped operations require the appropriate signing or recipient credentials. The certificate and private key must match, and encrypted private-key files require their password. The source representation selector controls how input text is interpreted. The output's T control identifies the CMS type; the displayed output itself is represented using the output format controls. Verification depends on the selected certificate and trust settings. Review the verification result before relying on a signed message.

docs.text: Public-Key Encrypt/Decrypt Dialog Guide The Public-Key Encrypt/Decrypt dialog encrypts data with a public key and decrypts it with the matching private key. It supports RSA, SM2, and ECDSA-based ECIES operations. Figure 1. Public-Key Encrypt/Decrypt dialog. Choose an operation, provide the data and corresponding key, then run it to view the result. Screen Areas Input Data — Enter the plaintext to encrypt or ciphertext to decrypt. Select its representation as Hex , String , or Base64 . The dialog shows the input length; C clears the input. Supported algorithms — RSA, SM2, and ECDSA. For ECDSA, this dialog uses ECIES encryption and decryption. Key source — Use a key managed by KeyPairMan or enable Use CertMan to choose certificate/key material from CertMan. The required key depends on the selected operation. Select each certificate and private key — Enable this option to specify a certificate or public-key file and a private-key file directly. Use Find to browse for a file. The adjacent V , D , and T controls view information, decode the file in the main BerEditor window, and show the key type, respectively. Encrypted PrivateKey / Password — Enable this when the selected private-key file is password protected, then enter its password. This applies when reading the private key for decryption. ECIES parameters — IV , Tag , and the other PublicKey value carry the ECIES parameters. On encryption, the dialog generates these values; on decryption, provide the values associated with the ciphertext. Values are hexadecimal. Encrypt / Decrypt — Select the operation. Encryption uses a public key; decryption uses the matching private key. RSA scheme — Choose V15 or OAEP for RSA. This setting does not select an SM2 or ECIES mode. Encrypt / Decrypt button — Runs the selected operation. The button label follows the selected mode. Output Data — Displays the result in the selected output representation ( Hex , String , or Base64 ) and shows its length. C clears the result. The up-arrow copies the result into Input Data and sets the input representation to match the output. Clear Data All — Clears the dialog's data and related values. Close closes the dialog. Encrypt Data Select Encrypt . Enter the plaintext in Input Data and choose its representation. Choose the public key or certificate source. If using individual files, enable Select each certificate and private key and select the certificate or public-key file. For RSA, select V15 or OAEP . For SM2 or ECDSA, use the appropriate public key; RSA scheme selection does not apply. Select Encrypt . The encrypted result appears in Output Data . For ECIES, record the generated IV , Tag , and other PublicKey value along with the ciphertext. Decryption requires these parameters. Decrypt Data Select Decrypt . Enter the ciphertext and choose its representation. Select the corresponding private key. If it is password protected, enable Encrypted PrivateKey and enter the password. For RSA, select the same padding scheme used to encrypt the data. For ECIES, enter the associated IV , Tag , and other PublicKey values in hexadecimal. Select Decrypt . The plaintext appears in Output Data . Notes Encryption and decryption must use a matching public/private key pair and compatible algorithm parameters. Keep the ECIES parameters with the ciphertext; the ciphertext alone is insufficient for this dialog's ECIES decryption workflow. The output representation controls how the result is displayed, not the cryptographic operation. Use the up-arrow to pass a result back as input. The dialog warns when input data, a required key, or a required password is missing, or when the selected data cannot be decoded in the chosen representation.

docs.text: SCEP Client Dialog Guide The SCEP Client creates and sends Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol requests to a CA. It supports certificate Issue , Update , and GetCRL operations, plus retrieval of the CA certificate. Figure 1. SCEP Client dialog with Issue selected. Use GetCA to retrieve CA certificate information, then create and send the selected request. Screen Areas SCEP URL — Enter or select the SCEP endpoint. Clear clears the saved URL list/input. Command / Make — Choose Issue , Update , or GetCRL , then select Make to build the corresponding request. Request — Displays the request in hexadecimal. Send transmits it to the SCEP endpoint. docs.text: Signature / Verify Dialog Guide The Signature / Verify dialog creates or verifies an asymmetric digital signature using input data or a file. Open it from Cryptography > Sign/Verify . Figure 1. Signature / Verify dialog. Select the data, signing key or verification certificate, algorithm options, and operation. Screen Areas Use KeyPairMan key / Use CertMan — Select the key source used when the individual certificate/private-key file group is not enabled. The selected manager provides the required key or certificate. Input Data / Input File — Enter message data directly or select a file to sign or verify. Input Type / Input area — Select the representation (such as Hex, String, or Base64), enter the data, and review the calculated length. In file mode, use Find and monitor file information and progress. Init / Update / Final / Reset — Perform signing or verification incrementally. Initialize with the chosen key, feed data blocks with Update, and complete the operation with Final. Select each certificate and private key — Enable this group to select the key material from files rather than a key manager. Cert or PubKey — Select a certificate or public key for verification. Find selects the file; V opens its details; D decodes it in BerEditor; T reports its key type. PrivateKey — Select the private key for signing. Find , V , D , and T provide file selection, details, BER decoding, and key-type information. Encrypted PrivateKey / Password — Select this when the private-key file is encrypted, then enter its password. Hash — Select a hash for RSA, ECDSA, DSA, and SM2 signatures. SM2 requires SM3. RSA Signature schemes — Select the RSA signature scheme, such as V15 or PSS, when signing or verifying with RSA. Sign / Verify — Select the operation. The run button changes to Sign or Verify . SignDigest — Signs or verifies an already-computed digest. The input must have the selected hash's digest length; the dialog warns if the lengths differ. Signature — Displays the generated signature in Hex when signing. For verification, enter the expected signature here as hexadecimal. The length is shown beside it. Clear Data All / Close — Clears input, key paths, signature and status, or closes the dialog. Sign a Message Select Input Data or Input File and provide the message. Select Sign . Choose a private key source: Use KeyPairMan key or CertMan from the top controls; or Enable Select each certificate and private key , then select a private key file. If it is encrypted, enable Encrypted PrivateKey and enter its password. Select the hash algorithm. For RSA, choose the RSA signature scheme as appropriate. Select Sign . The signature is displayed in hexadecimal. Verify a Signature Provide the same message data or file that was signed. Select Verify . Choose the public key source: a certificate or public key from the key manager, CertMan, or the file selection group. Choose the matching hash and RSA signature scheme. Enter the expected signature in the Signature field as hexadecimal. Select Verify and read the success or failure message. Sign or Verify a Digest Select SignDigest to operate directly on a precomputed digest rather than hashing a message through the normal Sign/Verify path. Enter the digest in the input area using the selected input representation. The dialog checks its length against the selected hash and asks whether to continue if they differ. Incremental Operations and Notes Use Init , Update , and Final to process data in stages. Select Reset before starting another staged operation. The same message bytes, key pair, hash, and RSA signature scheme must be used for successful verification. SM2 uses SM3. If another hash is selected, BerEditor prompts to switch to SM3. Some key algorithms do not support the staged Init/Update/Final workflow. Use the one-shot Sign or Verify action when prompted.

docs.text: SSL Check Dialog Guide The SSL Check dialog connects to an HTTPS server and reports TLS, certificate, and trust information. It can also test servers that require mutual TLS client authentication. Figure 1. SSL Check dialog on the Server tab. Enter a server URL and select Check to test the TLS connection and certificate chain. Screen Areas Server / Mutual tabs — Configure ordinary server checks on Server . Use Mutual to configure a client certificate and private key for mutual TLS. View Trust List / Use Mutual Auth — Open CertMan's trusted root list or enable client-certificate authentication. Protocol options — Check NO_SSLv3 , NO_TLSv1 , NO_TLSv1_1 , NO_TLSv1_2 , and NO_TLSv1_3 to disable the corresponding protocol versions for the test connection. Check Host Name — Enable hostname verification so the server certificate is checked against the requested host. Verify Mode / Verify Depth — Set the TLS certificate verification mode and maximum chain depth. The displayed default depth is 4. Trust CA — Optionally select a trusted CA certificate file with Find . V , D , and T view, decode, and identify the selected file. Fix Cipher — Enable a restricted cipher configuration, choose a TLS version and cipher, and select Add . Clear removes the configured cipher selection. URL / Check — Enter a hostname or URL and select Check . If no scheme is supplied, the dialog assumes https:// ; the default port is 443. C clears the URL field. Results table — Lists tested URL, port, certificate distinguished name, and expiry. Select or right-click a row for available certificate actions, including viewing, decoding, or checking it again. Clear URLs / Refresh — Clear the current result list or rerun checks for the saved URLs. SSL Tree and Log — Tree displays certificate authority/path information; Log shows connection and verification details. Clear Result clears results; Clear Log clears the log. Show Information / Close — Opens the selected server's SSL information window or closes the dialog. Check an HTTPS Server On the Server tab, configure protocol versions, hostname checking, verification mode, and verification depth as needed. Optionally select a Trust CA certificate or use the configured trust list. Enter a URL such as https://example.com , or a hostname such as example.com . Select Check . Review the result table, certificate tree, and log for connection and chain status. Select Show Information to inspect details for the selected result. Use Refresh to check saved URLs again. Check a Mutual TLS Server Enable Use Mutual Auth and open the Mutual tab. Provide the client CA certificate and select a client certificate/private-key pair, either from CertMan or with the individual certificate and private-key file controls. If the private key is encrypted, enable Encrypted PrivateKey and enter its password. Return to the server check and select Check . The client credentials are presented during the TLS handshake. Notes The URL check tests the live server connection using the current network, TLS, hostname, and trust settings. A server's configuration and certificate status can change over time. Disabling protocol versions or restricting ciphers changes the handshake options and may prevent connection to servers that do not support the remaining choices. Mutual TLS requires a client certificate and its matching private key. Keep private-key files and passwords confidential.
